usageNotes: Call this after the user completes the OpenID Connect authorization flow in the browser — it exchanges the authorization code for a PVE ticket and CSRF token. The `code`, `state`, and `redirect-url` must match exactly what the IdP returned and what was registered as the callback URL; a mismatch will cause the IdP to reject the code. The returned `ticket` and `CSRFPreventionToken` replace a standard username/password login for all subsequent API calls.

examples.summary: Exchange an OpenID authorization code for a PVE session ticket

tips: The OpenID realm must be configured in Datacenter > Permissions > Realms before this endpoint is usable.
Use the returned `CSRFPreventionToken` as the `CSRFPreventionToken` header on all subsequent write requests; omitting it will result in 401 errors.
The `redirect-url` must exactly match the value used when initiating the authorization request — even a trailing slash difference will cause verification to fail.
Permissions are `world` (no auth required to call this endpoint), since it is the authentication handshake itself.
The `cap` field in the response contains the caller's capability map, useful for client-side UI permission gating without a separate API call.
